solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English in lament isn't stirring, it's mawkish

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the fodder are churned into a new order

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for English, dropped into the fodder
its letters I, S, N, T are used without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone judges a lament with English lyrics to be unmoving and merely mawkish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like praise of the lament but is the anagram signal: E dropped 'in' LAMENT, plus ISNT, all shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe writing or feeling that is excessively and cloyingly emotional.

clue.text: Determined to promote new work trucks

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoting things raises them, so the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work in music
UTES is Australian and New Zealand slang for pickup trucks (utility vehicles)

explanation.surface: A firm resolves to advertise its new range of lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote' raises NOPUTES so it reads upward in the down light. UTE is Australian slang for a pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set upon a course is to be resolved or firmly bent on it, an idiomatic sense of determined.

clue.text: Fabric of part of the UK supported by almost nobody

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, and is held up by, the second

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, a constituent part of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: none means nobody, not one person

explanation.surface: A cloth from one region of Britain that hardly anyone buys.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts NI above NON (NONE cut short by 'almost').
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer silk or voile dress material, so it is an example of a fabric.

clue.text: Shuts in ascending spirit in house

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing upward means reading the assembled letters from the bottom
in places the spirit within the house

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Someone locks a ghost rising up inside a haunted house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost but is a drink. SEMI is British for a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: To immure someone is to wall them up or confine them, which is the same as shutting them in.

clue.text: Becomes involved in rerouting of eastern Ganges

indicators.note: rerouting a river sends it a different way, so these letters are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets drawn into a scheme to divert the Ganges in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rerouting of' shuffles E plus GANGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage in something is to take part or get involved, so engages is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Will volunteers set upon workers in experiment?

indicators.note: in tells us the volunteers and workers go inside the experiment

parts.note: a test is an experiment or trial

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece set upon another sits directly above it

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A question of whether volunteers will turn on the workers during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is not the verb but the legal document. The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of property after death, so the two words name the same thing.

clue.text: Escape from Welsh icon on radio — not fashionable

indicators.note: a word heard on the radio is only spoken, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: the leek is a national emblem of Wales
out means unfashionable, the opposite of in

explanation.surface: A broadcast about getting away from a dated symbol of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' gives the sound of LEEK, the Welsh national emblem, spelt LEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: When information or gas leaks out it escapes, so the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: With gold award, mark author's true identity

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a Tony is an American theatre award
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: A writer reveals their real name on winning a gold medal and other honours.
explanation.definitionFit: An autonym is a book published under the writer's real name, or that real name itself, as opposed to a pseudonym.

clue.text: Graphical representation about Spain suppressing old island group

indicators.note: about means the mixed letters go around the Spanish piece
a representation here is a re-presentation, the letters of the word presented afresh in another order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain (España)
O is a standard abbreviation for old; in a down clue the Spanish letter is set above, suppressing it

explanation.surface: A chart showing that Spain held down an old cluster of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' shuffles GRAPHICAL; 'about' wraps that round E, and 'suppressing' sets it above O in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago is a chain or cluster of islands, such as the Canaries.

clue.text: Some suggest altering organised unit

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people propose reorganising a team.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology a gestalt is a whole whose organised structure is more than the sum of its parts.

clue.text: Pay attention to dog that's taken second in Crufts, fashionable creature

indicators.note: the first piece takes in, or swallows, the selected letter

parts.note: to tend something is to look after it or attend to it

indicators.note: second in picks out the word's second letter

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: An instruction to look closely at the stylish dog that came second at Crufts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's taken' puts R ('second in' Crufts) inside TEND. Crufts is Britain's biggest dog show.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter is a person whose style others copy, a leader of fashion.

clue.text: Bird's not bare-headed

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel fattened for the table
split three and two, wearing headgear

explanation.surface: An observation that a fowl is wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a domestic bird, while the split phrase literally describes someone whose head is covered.

clue.text: Long-winded account of Mr Al Gore travelling around Italy

indicators.note: around tells us the mixed letters surround the single letter
travelling letters move about and arrive in a different order

parts.note: I is the international vehicle registration code for Italy

explanation.surface: A tedious story about Al Gore's tour through Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' shuffles MRALGORE and 'around' puts that about I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a lengthy, rambling story or a tiresome, complicated procedure.

clue.text: Pays no attention to topless ladies in Naples sun

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the word's first letter

parts.note: signore is the Italian for ladies, plural of signora
S is the abbreviation for sun, as in weather maps or days of the week

explanation.surface: Someone averts their gaze from bare-chested sunbathers in Naples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the first S of SIGNORE, Italian for ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them, which is exactly paying them no heed.

clue.text: A touch of lemon in mixed puree is coming across very disgusting

indicators.note: coming across means crossing into the mixed letters, so the next piece goes inside them
mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged
a touch is a small amount, here the opening letter

explanation.surface: A chef's verdict that a lemony puree is revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram ('mixed') gives REPULSIE, which V then cuts into. 'very' supplies V, so the definition is just 'disgusting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive arouses revulsion, so it is nauseating in the same way.

clue.text: Express dispatched journalist, in essence, perhaps

indicators.note: to express a word is to say it, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: sent means dispatched, posted off
ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter was sent off by express delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a newspaper or delivery service; it signals the sound of SENT, spelt SCENT. 'perhaps' marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is a perfume, so anything soaked in it smells of it, an example of being perfumed.

clue.text: Crawling pest eating tips of yellow eglantine carries over plant disease

indicators.note: crawling suggests slow wriggling movement, so the letters squirm into a new order

parts.note: the pest's own four letters, eating up the letters that follow so they join its pool

indicators.note: tips of takes the first letter of each word

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, which the pest carries along with it

explanation.surface: A crawling insect devouring a yellow wild rose spreads blight around.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the shuffled pest is 'eating' Y and E at one spot and 'carries' O at another; pooling all seven letters gives the same result. Eglantine is the sweet-briar, a wild rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyespot is a fungal infection of cereals and other crops that leaves eye-shaped lesions.

clue.text: Issue of rising character in Athens with reputation

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upward, from the bottom

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a good name is a good reputation

explanation.surface: A question of an up-and-coming Athenian figure with a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ETA plus NAME upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, as a verb.

clue.text: Part of Constable autumn scene

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A detail from one of John Constable's autumn landscape paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is the English landscape painter, which makes 'scene' read as a painted view.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque group or striking arrangement, a vivid view or picture.

clue.text: Going to great lengths, former tenor joins regiment

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
T is the abbreviation for tenor in vocal music
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A singer who used to be a tenor enlists in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme measures go far beyond the ordinary, which is going as far as possible.

clue.text: In retirement, professors deserve to be surrounded by erudition and intellect principally

indicators.note: the next piece is placed in the middle, enclosed by the following letters
principally takes the first letter of each word

parts.note: to merit something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Retired academics deserve to be ringed by learning and intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be surrounded by' puts MERIT between E and I, the 'principally' letters of erudition and intellect.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are retired professors who keep their title as an honour; the Latin plural.

clue.text: English copper in East End owned gold in SA republic

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the Cockney accent of London's East End drops the H

parts.note: had means owned
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: An English policeman in London's East End owned gold in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: East End Cockneys famously drop their Hs, so HAD becomes 'AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a republic on the Pacific coast of South America.

clue.text: Take advantage with beer in barrel? The reverse: it's on tap

indicators.note: with joins the next piece to this one

parts.note: to avail oneself of something is to take advantage of it

indicators.note: in signals one piece inside another
the reverse swaps the roles, so the barrel goes into the beer instead

parts.note: ale is a beer

explanation.surface: Use a keg of beer; then the line that the beer is on draught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beer in barrel' would put ALE inside B; 'The reverse' flips this so B goes 'in' ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is ready whenever wanted, which is what being accessible means.

clue.text: Vineyard's given good man livelihood

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine of recognised quality
ST, saint, is a holy or good man

explanation.surface: A wine estate has been handed to a decent man to make a living.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'earns a crust' in British idiom, meaning earns a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A crust is a living, from the idiom earning a crust: one's daily bread.

clue.text: Midlands city loses attempt to have witches gathering

indicators.note: loses means a piece is dropped from the city name

parts.note: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A Midlands city gives up its bid to host a meeting of witches.
explanation.walkthrough: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is an assembly or company of witches, traditionally thirteen.

clue.text: Stone-like, old, old man is with band

parts.note: pa is a colloquial word for father, one's old man
a line is a band or stripe

explanation.surface: A description of an elderly father in a band, as solid as stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' is slang for father, giving PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline means resembling opal, the milky iridescent gemstone, so it describes something like a stone.

clue.text: Driven wildly round area, the last to arrive here was Norman

definitions.text: the last to arrive here was Norman

indicators.note: round means the mixed letters go round the next piece
wildly signals the letters fly about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone drove wildly around a neighbourhood, recalling the Norman Conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' shuffles DRIVEN and 'round' wraps it about A. The definition recalls 1066, the last successful invasion of England, by the Normans.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror's Normans were the most recent force to conquer England by attack, making them its latest such arrival.

clue.text: One's paid to polish off performance by Queen

parts.note: the execution of a piece is its performance
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A paid worker finishes off a show starring the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polish off' means kill, not tidy up. ER = Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman or headsman is paid to kill condemned people, and polish off is slang for killing.
